original_question: In the setting of Conjecture 4.1, can one always choose the iterate n to be 1? That is, for every z in Ext_P^{s,t}(F_p, F_p), is P^0 z already nilpotent after a single application of P^0?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 4.3 in Section 4, which is the paper’s explicit sharpening of Conjecture 4.1. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly targets John H. Palmieri’s Section 4 problem, uses the right Ext group and the operator P^0, and asks exactly whether the existential iterate n from Conjecture 4.1 can be replaced by n=1—the separate strengthening recorded in the paper as Conjecture 4.3. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
missing_details: The ambient prime should be stated explicitly: let p be a prime. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))

The algebra P should be defined: P is the dual of the polynomial part P_* ≅ F_p[ξ_1, ξ_2, ξ_3, ...] of the dual Steenrod algebra; when p=2, P is the mod-2 Steenrod algebra, and for odd p it is a quotient Hopf algebra of the mod-p Steenrod algebra. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
The filtration variable should be quantified as in Conjecture 4.1: fix s>0. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
The internal degree t is arbitrary and should be quantified, with z understood to be homogeneous of bidegree (s,t). ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))

The operator P^0 should be defined, not just named: it is the algebra endomorphism on Ext induced by the p-th power map on P_*, and it has degree behavior P^0: Ext_P^{s,t}(F_p,F_p) -> Ext_P^{s,pt}(F_p,F_p). ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
The nilpotence condition should specify the ambient algebra: P^0 z is to be nilpotent in the bigraded algebra Ext_P^{*,*}(F_p,F_p). ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))

To stay paper-faithful, the question should be presented as Conjecture 4.3 itself, rather than only as an informal variant 'in the setting of Conjecture 4.1'. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
refined_question: Let p be a prime, let P_* be the polynomial part of the dual Steenrod algebra with P_* ≅ F_p[ξ_1, ξ_2, ξ_3, ...], and let P be its dual Hopf algebra. Fix s>0. Is it true that for every internal degree t and every homogeneous class z in Ext_P^{s,t}(F_p,F_p), the class P^0 z in Ext_P^{s,pt}(F_p,F_p) is nilpotent in the bigraded algebra Ext_P^{*,*}(F_p,F_p), where P^0 is the algebra endomorphism induced by the p-th power map on P_*? ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
justification: Section 4 first defines the exact ambient objects: a prime p, the Hopf algebra P dual to the polynomial part of the dual Steenrod algebra, and the endomorphism P^0 on Ext induced by the p-th power map on P_* (journal p. 438). It then states Conjecture 4.1 as an eventual-nilpotence assertion in fixed filtration s>0, notes in Theorem 4.2 that Conjecture 4.1 is true when p=2, and immediately records the sharper question suggested by hand and computer calculations when p=2 as Conjecture 4.3 (journal p. 439). Since your draft asks exactly whether one may always take n=1, the nearest official formulation is Conjecture 4.3, not the broader Conjecture 4.1. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
